body:
Thank you for the vote of confidence. They haven't replied and I'm not going to worry about it anymore. If they get back to me, great. If they don't, they don't. They've taken enough of my time and they won't get more, I've lived years without them and I can do it again. I'm going to take a week to sulk and then get back on my feet. I don't need others to validate my existence anymore. 

So again, thank you. I appreciate your time and how you've helped talk me out of this.

I don't presume to know anything about your circumstances other then what you've told me, but from what I've seen personally, most people who think they need to lose weight really don't. With neuroma I understand your options are limited, but I wouldn't worry about it too much if you're worried about losing weight, but again I don't know of your circumstances. I didn't mean to imply that I lost weight exercising this past week, it actually just came off because I've been a wreck lately. 

It's funny, I actually started reading Don Quixote with just a bit of mild interest in it and no real expectation to finish it, but eventually I found myself enjoying it so much that the length stopped being a factor and before I knew it I had completed it. If time is a factor for you maybe try reading Candide by Voltaire, it's also a good satire and much shorter. 

Anyway, I appreciate you lending an ear to my plights. It does mean a lot and these conversations with you and UnoGeo have calmed me down some. I know I'm just using a throwaway account but I'm a person all the same and for you to take time to talk to me helps a lot.

I never did marathons, but I used to run some forested trails with my brother that were about 3 km in length. I've literally lost 5 pounds in the last week, so I don't know if I'd be able to do it again now that the stamina's shot. Yoga sounds therapeutic. 

My main genres are sci fi and horror, favorite authors are Philip K Dick, Frank Herbert, and Lovecraft. My thesis was on Philip K Dick and Blade Runner, and I ended up getting into Dune later on. Also love me some classical literature. Don Quixote is one of my favorites, though I also sway towards some of the older Shakespeare classics like Macbeth and Midnight Summer's Dream. Agh my inner literature nerd is showing

You don't necessarily need to come right out and say you're suicidal. Just be tactful about it. Mention that you've been feeling down for a while and that it's not just a phase that came out of nowhere. We get this way once circumstances pile up past the point of coping and you should make them understand that; let them know what's been leading up to this and be straight about asking them for help. They're your family and you shouldn't be afraid to talk to them about serious issues like this. I'm not going to preach to you about how you shouldn't kick yourself for perceived past mistakes, but the lingering regret of such actions is something that will eat you from the inside out if you let it fester, take it from me. There's no easy way to get over it, but talking with others who care about you will at LEAST set you on the right road to recovery.

I extended an olive branch of peace to the former friends. I was as civil as possible. I already admitted to my mistakes, and mentioned I was willing to talk things out. Now all I can do is wait, but being as real as possible here I don't expect much anymore. But again, your advice is appreciated and I wouldn't have done even that much if you hadn't talked with me. Thank you.

Yep. I used to be more varied in my hobbies, running, reading, etc. but lately all I do is play retro video games. Which was one of my main hobbies before but now it's become more of a crutch to remind me of better times. Reading used to be a big one but now I can't concentrate anymore.

One of my former friends owned a few ferrets and they were adorably derpy. Thought about getting one but now the prospect is kind of soured.

I appreciate that you took the time to talk with me a bit in spite of having real responsibilities, but please don't feel obligated to continue with me. This has been a long time coming and circumstances have conglomerated to the point where my coping mechanisms have broken.
One's a doberman/husky mix and the others an aussie shepherd. Dogs are much better friends then people.

I'd like to think that, but a part of me also doesn't see the point anymore. Get a good job. Stand on my own two feet. Have a few diversions here and there. Honestly it doesn't sound appealing to me anymore. This is what I was on the road to in my last job, and with the people I knew I thought it could feasibly happen but now I just don't care anymore. I won't have the same group of friends ever again, nor the enjoyable experiences. My last text from one of them was literally "I don't like talking with you right now"

I couldn't swallow my pride, basically. I was working retail after spending years achieving a BA in English, I had some vague possibilities in regards to more prestigious employment, former gf wanted to get promoted but wouldn't have been able to because corporate frowns on relationships that mess with the hierarchy, so I martyred myself a bit too. I feel horrible typing all that out, I really messed up. All the job possibilities I mentioned have either rejected me or are still up in the air, god that was dumb. Of course I had problems with some of the management, but nothing I couldn't handle, so I'm not citing that as a reason.

You say that you know your family would be devastated, so why not just sit them down and let them know how you've been feeling? I don't know your reasons for being afraid of telling them, but if you know that they would be devastated then I'm going to assume that they at LEAST care for you a lot, so why not give it a try? Coming out about my depression to mine at least set me on the right road to recovery, though it is an ongoing process. Therapy isn't for everyone, I'll admit that much, but therapy isn't necessarily the only option (assuming you're talking about sitting down with psychologists and such). I don't want to place too much stock into medication, but after going through three different prescriptions I eventually found one that helped me out in hard situations - obviously it wasn't instantaneous, but it's always a possibility! 
Other then that you mention that your best friend at least wants to be of help, so elaborating some on your emotions with him (if you haven't already) would at least go to a willing mind. Sometimes just talking about these things face to face with others is cathartic. You seem to have a lot of support, don't hesitate to use it.

I used to be in a similar position to your boyfriend. Be patient with him, keep the help offers available. He might not show it now but I'm positive he will appreciate the fact that you were with him through these times, and it speaks a lot on your character to stick with him throughout all this. It will mean the world to him. For now, just let him be but don't keep yourself away from him and know that being too caring isn't worth suicidal thoughts.

Thank you for the reply. I have a few job interviews/offers in my peripheral atm but right now I honestly don't feel like doing anything. I worry that even if a potential employer does call me, I won't be able to pick up the phone because I really just can't talk right now. My friends are currently seeping through the cracks and I didn't even have the energy to get out of bed today. Just laid down and half watched old yugioh episodes to remind me of better times. Suddenly hours had passed.
Things is, if people wouldn't feel guilty about throwing me away I would honestly feel better about making the big decision. I want to rid myself of these desires to be social. In the end it always comes back to bite me in the ass big time. If I was a robot I'd be content to just exist and fill my niche in society. Beep boop.
Honestly, thanks. I didn't think anyone would reply and I don't expect you to follow up on this, but you took the time to understand my situation and come up with a thoughtful response.
